authoredSolutions.51: Summing the terms gives \(nx^2+n(n+1)x+\left[\frac{(n-1)n(2n-1)}{6}+n(n-1)\right]=4n\). Dividing by \(n\) yields a quadratic \(x^2+(n+1)x+C=0\) whose roots differ by 2, so its discriminant equals 4. This forces \(n^2=49\Rightarrow n=7\). Sum of roots \(2\alpha+2=-(n+1)=-8\Rightarrow\alpha=-5\). Hence \(n+\alpha=2\).

Then \((B-A)(B+A)=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4&5\\5&5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}13&15\\7&10\end{bmatrix}\), whose transpose is \(\begin{bmatrix}13&7\\15&10\end{bmatrix}\ne\) the given matrix, so S1 is wrong. \(\det(\operatorname{adj}(A+B))=\det(A+B)=\det\begin{bmatrix}4&5\\5&5\end{bmatrix}=-5\), so S2 is correct.
